clue.text: Local nuclear supply beset by endless change

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: VARY means change; it loses its last letter

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A community's nuclear power supply is besieged by constant policy changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun about power, but here it is the adverb formed from supple. 'Endless change' splits in two, and its pieces sit on either side of the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernacular describes the everyday speech or style native to a particular region, so it works as an adjective meaning local.

clue.text: Nothing omitted in utter depravity

indicators.note: something omitted is left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to utter is to voice something
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Total moral corruption where nothing is held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' poses as an adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb to voice; take O out of VOICE to leave VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice is wicked or immoral behaviour, a close synonym for moral corruption or depravity.

clue.text: Ruins revolutionary video game company Virginia runs

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the following letters run backwards

parts.note: Sega is the Japanese video game maker
VA is the US state abbreviation
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A games company based in Virginia is hit by damaging rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruins' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb; the whole string SEGA, VA, R is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravage is to devastate or wreck something, so ravages and ruins are verb synonyms in the third person.

clue.text: Notwithstanding conserving energy, this teammate is struggling

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep and hold on to, so one letter is held inside the rest
a struggling side is in disarray, so its letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Even though this player is saving their strength, they are still having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: Add E to the twelve letters of 'this teammate' and rearrange all thirteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a concession meaning nevertheless or however, as in 'it is cheap; at the same time, it is ugly'.

clue.text: Rare to miss the German Open

indicators.note: to miss something is to go without it, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: rare meat is underdone
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A rare occurrence: someone fails to make the German Open golf tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' suggests unusual, but it is the cooking sense; 'German Open' reads as a sporting event, but 'Open' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A button or zip that has been undone is unfastened, so undone is an adjective synonym for open.

clue.text: Look, Mike and Dennis for example supporting current reward scheme

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece is placed below the next one

parts.note: an air is a look or manner
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the physics symbol for electric current
Les Dennis is a British TV presenter and comedian

explanation.surface: A group of men endorsing a loyalty programme from an energy company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dennis for example' points to a surname, so the solver needs a man called Dennis: Les Dennis, long-time host of the British game show Family Fortunes. In a down clue LES goes beneath I.
explanation.definitionFit: Air Miles is a British loyalty programme in which shoppers collect points redeemable for flights, so it is a reward scheme.

clue.text: Probability of extra term in class

parts.note: an odd one is extra, left over

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so the final letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A school wonders how likely it is that an extra term will be added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' reads as a school period, but it means the end, so take the last letter of 'class'.
explanation.definitionFit: The odds are the likelihood or chance of something happening, so the plural noun means probability.

clue.text: Harry unloaded Dormobile seconds before Helen's home?

indicators.note: with the load taken out only the shell is left, so just the outer letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
S is the abbreviation for seconds
Helen of Troy, from Greek legend

explanation.surface: Prince Harry empties his camper van just before arriving at Helen's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name, but it is the verb to harass. A Dormobile is a British camper van brand.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to ravage or lay waste, as raiders harried a coast, which matches destroy in its older sense.

clue.text: Unity of purpose in policing daily riots

indicators.note: policing brings disorder under control, so these letters are marshalled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Police show a common resolve in dealing with riots that break out every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riots' sounds like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'policing' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidarity is mutual support and agreement among members of a group sharing a common aim or cause.

clue.text: Longed for school to welcome experienced US soldier

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in the US a coed is a co-educational school or college
a vet is an American veteran

explanation.surface: A school is eager to welcome back a war veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' serves both pieces: coed and vet are both American usages.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to desire something intensely, often what belongs to another, so coveted means wanted or yearned for.

clue.text: No trouble mostly filling concrete

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter goes
a filling is put inside something else, like a sandwich

parts.note: concrete things are real and tangible
FUSS is trouble or bother, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Pouring concrete went mostly without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' reads as the building material, but it is the adjective meaning tangible. 'No' as a noun is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A no is a refusal, as in 'the answer was a firm no', so both are nouns for a negative reply.

clue.text: Possible appearance of Bow villain on EastEnders?

indicators.note: the speech of East Londoners is meant, so the words are said in a Cockney accent

parts.note: a villain is a figure of hate; a Cockney drops the H

explanation.surface: How a baddie from the soap set in East London might look, Bow being a district there.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, where Bow is; but the bow is a tied ribbon, and Cockney 'ate' is said like eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow knot with its two loops seen from the front traces the shape of an eight drawn on its side.

clue.text: Politician identified as having success encouraging growth?

parts.note: a member of the Green Party
to finger someone is to identify them to the police

explanation.surface: A politician is named for successfully promoting economic growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests the economy, but it is plants in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A green-fingered person is a skilled gardener whose plants thrive, so the adjective describes success at nurturing plants.

clue.text: Ruthless devil, American guy around fifty

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it, so the pieces surround another letter

parts.note: an imp is a small devil
A is a standard abbreviation for American
a guy is a supporting rope or cable
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A cruel demon, a middle-aged American man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it means a guy rope, which holds a tent or mast steady. 'Around' applies to everything before fifty, so the Roman numeral ends up inside, just after the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: An implacable person cannot be appeased or softened, so the adjective overlaps with merciless and unrelenting.

clue.text: Capital essential to maintain account after retiring

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a must is an essential

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Money needed to keep an account going once someone stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'account' suggest finance, and 'retiring' suggests a pension, but the capital is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital city of Oman, on the Arabian Peninsula's eastern coast.

clue.text: Covering year roughly, lay right type of grass

indicators.note: to cover is to lie over or ahead of something, so this piece comes first

parts.note: to lay money is to bet it

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, so the letters only loosely keep their order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions on laying down the right kind of turf to cover the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like lawn, but it is British slang for an informer; the betting pieces come ahead of the rearranged YEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is someone who informs on associates to police, which is one kind of traitor.

clue.text: Son, playing his part creating spacecraft

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: playing about with something rearranges it, so the letters are moved

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy acts in a school play about building a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing his part' reads as acting a role; 'playing' is the signal and 'his part' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A starship is a science-fiction vessel built to travel between stars, a type of spacecraft.

clue.text: Text flipping trainspotter Billy receives

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters read backwards
to receive is to take in, so the clue words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A trainspotter called Billy gets an annoying message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word, as in 'flipping text', but it is the signal to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written words of an opera or musical, the text that the music is set to.

clue.text: Syrian perhaps from the South purchases leading coffee-maker

indicators.note: purchasing something means taking hold of it, so one piece holds another
in a down clue reading from the bottom means going upwards, backwards

parts.note: a Syrian is an example of an Arab
leading is first, written 1ST and read as IST

explanation.surface: A Syrian buys a top coffee machine imported from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 is read as the letter I, a common crossword trick, so 1ST gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista is a person who prepares and serves espresso drinks in a café, someone who makes coffee.

clue.text: Tried giving up cigarettes finally for new love

indicators.note: to give something up is to hand it over, so one letter is swapped out

parts.note: to have tried or attempted is to have sought

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the last letter of the word
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone attempted quitting smoking for the sake of a new partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis score for zero, and 'for' tells you N replaces S.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is the tennis term for a zero score, and nought is another word for zero.

clue.text: Hereditary information on name that's turned up

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: turned upwards in a down clue means the letters climb, running backwards

parts.note: to name something is to cite it

explanation.surface: Data about a family name that emerged in research.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts GEN above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic traits are passed down through genes from parents to offspring, so the adjective means inherited.

clue.text: Blair, say, essentially glib individual given leadership of Labour?

indicators.note: the essence is at the core, so the middle letters are taken

parts.note: the middle two letters of the word
one is a single individual

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Tony Blair as a smooth talker taking charge of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious Blair is the former prime minister, but the definition wants another Blair by first name: the dancer and entertainer Lionel Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Blair was a British dancer and TV personality, so his first name is an example of a Blair.

clue.text: Ex-PM's wife with concern over King's former method of communication

parts.note: Carrie Johnson is the wife of Boris Johnson
R for Rex, king
'not my pigeon' means not my concern

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson's wife is worried about how the King used to send messages.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was UK prime minister from 2019 to 2022. 'Not my pigeon' is a British idiom for 'not my concern'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homing pigeons carried messages tied to their legs, notably in wartime, long before modern telecommunications.

clue.text: Tie up puppy maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to close or settle a deal
second meaning: an animal whose young are called pups

explanation.walkthrough: 'Puppy' suggests a dog, but a baby seal is also a pup, so 'maybe' marks the parent animal as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To seal an agreement is to finalise it, and seals are marine mammals whose babies are also called pups.

clue.text: Ask Europeans on vacation to cut wood

indicators.note: a cut goes into something, so one piece is inserted into another

parts.note: beech is a type of tree and timber

indicators.note: a vacated place has been emptied, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Holidaying Europeans are asked to chop down trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' sounds like being on holiday, but it means emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to implore or beg earnestly, a more pleading way to ask for something.

clue.text: Man, old Pip, repeatedly removing top garment

indicators.note: taking the top off again and again means each of the two pieces loses its first letter

parts.note: a knight is a chess man
to pip, in dated British slang, is to die

explanation.surface: An old fellow called Pip keeps taking off his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pip' looks like the Dickens hero, but it is a dated verb meaning to die; knight and die both lose their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a loose nightdress worn in bed, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Energetic style of road cycling

indicators.note: a cycle goes round, so a letter moves from one end to the other

parts.note: a lane is a minor road

explanation.surface: Riding a bike on the road with vigour and flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' fits the road scene but means rotating: LANE's final E moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan is vigour, flair and spirited enthusiasm, a lively and stylish manner.

clue.text: Having no interest in parties?

parts.note: surface reading: someone who avoids celebrations and social gatherings
setter's reading: political parties, so someone indifferent to politics

explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' suggests celebrations; the question mark warns that the political sense is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An apolitical person is not interested or involved in politics, and so cares nothing for political organisations.
